rules.rationale: Dense O/N centers donate and accept multiple water hydrogen bonds, the dominant favorable term in hydration free energy.
Pure saturated hydrocarbons offer no polar contacts; cavity-formation cost dominates, giving weakest hydration.
Heavily halogenated solutes are bulky and weakly hydrogen bonding, historically poorly hydrated despite high polarizability.
Intermediate heteroatom counts retain hydrogen-bond capacity; graded polarity term stabilizes the surrogate across 91 candidates.

skill.hypothesis: Hydration affinity tracks polar hydrogen-bonding surface, so graded heteroatom content leads while apolar and polyhalogenated solutes are penalized. Fails if the score instead rewards hydrophobic bulk or halogen polarizability.

rules.rationale: Source ESOL evidence gave smiles_short a positive effect (+6.89, n=261); small solutes favored solvation.
Strongest source value prior (-11.46, confidence 0.47): large lipophilic solutes lose solvation favorability.
Source hbond_donor_bin maps onto target hetero_atom_bin (transfer weight 0.51); donor richness drove favorable source effects.
Counter-hypothesis: reverses the low-confidence source smiles_mid penalty, since mid-size polar solutes accumulate hydration sites.

skill.hypothesis: Transfers the explicit ESOL size priors plus the donor-to-heteroatom role, but flips the weakest mid-length term. Fails if FreeSolv hydration magnitude grows with polar surface area rather than shrinking with molecular size.
